chunks: Ali (ibn al-Hakam) from his father from Ibn Abi Najran from Safwan from al-Kahili from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the tailor (or cleaner) to whom a garment is entrusted, with a condition that he return it at a specific time. He said: 'If he delays and the garment is lost after the time, he is liable (for its value).'

key_terms.اَلْقَصَّارُ: Tailor or cleaner (one who cleans/dyes cloth)
key_terms.اُشْتُرِطَ عَلَيْهِ: A condition was stipulated upon him

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if an entrusted item is lost after the agreed time has passed?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the transition from *daman al-amanah* (liability for loss in trust) to *daman al-ghasb* (liability for usurpation/delay) in commercial contracts. It establishes that exceeding the stipulated deadline constitutes a breach of contract, rendering the custodian strictly liable for any subsequent loss, a principle foundational to Shia jurisprudence on *ijarah* (hire) and *qard* (loan).
